judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence excluding insureds as to current or past partnerships not shown in the Declarations; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section II.1's entity-based grants, though it sharpens the Declarations' description of the insured entity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general anti-stacking rule listing three irrelevancies; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Governs the specific limits that follow, all of which are expressed as 'subject to' it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the General Aggregate as the sum of three heads with a products-completed carve-out; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with the Declarations note that products-completed operations are included subject to the General Aggregate Limit and with definition V.16.b.(3).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence aggregate for the defined hazard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any one person or organization' is a defined measuring unit; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressed as subject to the General Aggregate, matching Section III.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each Occurrence Limit tied to 'all bodily injury and property damage arising out of any one occurrence'; the occurrence-counting question is latent but the wording is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 'occurrence' definition and the aggregate limits above it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any one premises, while rented to you, or in the case of damage by fire, while rented to you or temporarily occupied by you' compresses two different triggers into one sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Medical Expense Limit per person; a single clear rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Coverage C grant and the Declarations figure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The annual-period rule with its extension proviso is intricate but expressly worked out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applies to the aggregate limits above it and matches the one-year policy period in the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence preserving the insurer's obligations on bankruptcy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision; consistent with Legal Action Against Us.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practicable' is elastic and frequently litigated, though the notice contents are enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the property-side Duties In The Event Of Loss and to the Legal Action condition requiring full compliance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unless all of its terms have been fully complied with' plus the agreed-settlement definition; strong but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contains no limitation period, unlike the property conditions and CP 01 01 A, but that difference is deliberate across coverage parts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long excess-insurance provision with enumerated categories and a sharing formula; complex but explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to 'Exclusion g. of Section I — Coverage A' matches the aircraft/auto/watercraft exclusion as lettered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Equal shares then limits; a fully specified algorithm.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with the primary and excess paragraphs of the same condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deposit premium, audit computation and record-keeping duties are each stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Declarations note that the liability premium is subject to audit and the Calculation of Premium endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three short representations; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside the concealment/misrepresentation conditions as amended by IL 01 60, which govern the consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Severability of interests stated in two limbs with an express limits carve-out; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its interaction with 'any insured' exclusions elsewhere is the classic point, but the carve-out language is explicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subrogation with a duty not to impair rights; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike the property-side condition it contains no pre-loss waiver permission, a deliberate difference between coverage parts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not less than 30 days before the expiration date' is a precise figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 02 61 B requires 60 days' nonrenewal notice with reasons and supersedes any condition to the contrary, so two different notice periods appear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Advertisement' is defined with express treatment of internet material; workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the Coverage B exclusions and definition 14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Auto' defined by exclusion of 'mobile equipment'; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complementary to the mobile equipment definition, which reciprocally deems certain vehicles autos.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Bodily injury means bodily injury, sickness or disease' is circular and famously silent on emotional distress.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives Coverages A and C and the employment-practices exclusion; no internal contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-part territory with a merits-determination proviso; detailed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is broader than the property-side coverage territory, but the two govern different coverage parts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Employee includes a leased worker' but not a temporary worker; a short deeming rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the leased and temporary worker definitions and the employer's liability exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Officer positions created by charter, by-laws 'or any other similar governing document'; a general phrase, but narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Section II.1.c-d, which treats managers of an LLC separately from executive officers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'One which becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be' is compact but has been construed elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the pollution exclusion carve-outs, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb definition with a restoration proviso; intricate but complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches exclusions m. and n., which use it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lettered list ending in the broad paragraph f. ('that part of any other contract... under which you assume the tort liability of another'), with three carve-outs; the general/specific tension is real.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge of the contractual liability exclusion and the Supplementary Payments indemnitee provision, both of which reference it expressly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Leased worker defined by reference to a labour leasing firm agreement; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the employee and temporary worker definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three temporal limbs plus a mechanical-device exception; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the auto exclusion and the products-completed operations hazard consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A six-paragraph typology with a deeming proviso turning some self-propelled vehicles into autos; long but closely specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reciprocal with the 'auto' definition and the mobile equipment exclusions; the cross-references line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'An accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions' defines a word by an undefined word; heavily litigated generally.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It underpins the Each Occurrence Limit and the Coverage A trigger, which are consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The seven enumerated offences include 'wrongful eviction from, wrongful entry into, or invasion of the right of private occupancy of a room, dwelling or premises', wording that is squarely engaged by an apartment landlord's conduct and often disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the Coverage B exclusions and the employment-practices endorsement, which carve conduct back out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The broad 'pollutants' definition again; open at the edges but identical to industry wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the property-side definitions, so the instrument is internally consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The completion rules and the three exclusions are detailed, but paragraph b.(3) makes the hazard turn on what the Declarations classification says.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations classifications do state that products-completed operations are subject to the General Aggregate Limit, which by b.(3) removes those operations from the hazard while Section III.3 still provides a separate aggregate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Physical injury to tangible property' plus loss of use, with electronic data deemed not tangible; standard but perennially construed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Damage To Property exclusion and the impaired property definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Suit' defined to include arbitration and other ADR with consent; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with the duty to defend in Coverages A and B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substitute for a permanent employee 'or to meet seasonal or short-term workload conditions'; the boundary is soft but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements the employee and leased worker definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Volunteer worker defined by absence of compensation and direction by the insured; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section II.2.a and the Coverage C 'any insured' exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A non-standard exclusion built on six numbered heads, the last two of which are open catch-alls ('any supervision, instructions, recommendations, warnings or advice' and any obligation to share damages).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the pollution exclusion and the lead endorsement without any priority rule, though the overlaps point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion lists employment-related practices 'such as coercion, demotion, evaluation, reassignment, discipline, defamation, harassment, humiliation or discrimination', an illustrative list whose outer reach is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same illustrative 'such as' list, applied to personal and advertising injury; the same open-ended quality.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes conduct otherwise covered by definition 14's defamation limb, an intended interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'would not have occurred, in whole or in part, but for' formula with an anti-concurrent tail; broad but explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Uses the endorsement's own 'fungi' definition and parallels the property-side fungus exclusion and Limited Coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sampled text is heavily corrupted, with words missing from the operative 'would not have taken place' clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the Coverage A version, so its intended effect can be reconstructed from the companion paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definition of 'fungi' including mould, mildew, mycotoxins and by-products.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Substantively identical to the property forms' 'fungus' definition, differing only in the defined word.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad lead exclusion whose paragraph 3.c-d extend to 'any supervision, instructions, recommendations, warnings or advice' and any sharing obligation, catch-alls of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps the pollution and asbestos exclusions without a priority rule, but all point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is conditioned on one of three enumerated nuclear/biological/chemical attributes; specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any injury or damage' is defined inclusively ('includes but is not limited to'), leaving the class open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Some of the listed terms ('environmental damage', 'injury') are not defined in any coverage part attached here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory certified-act definition with two criteria; precise by incorporation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A negative definition with a 72-hour aggregation rule; convoluted but complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the certified-act definition and with IL 09 60 A.2 on the property side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence confirming that non-excluded terrorism does not create coverage for otherwise excluded loss.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to IL 09 60 D on the property side; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb war exclusion applying 'however caused, arising, directly or indirectly'; broad but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces printed Exclusion i., which is expressly limited to contractually assumed liability, so both versions appear in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same three limbs applied to personal and advertising injury; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a war exclusion to Coverage B, which the base form lacked — an addition rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes punitive damages arising out of a certified act of terrorism; a single clear rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the terrorism cap provisions elsewhere in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory certified-act definition repeated; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the definitions in IL 09 60 and CG 21 72, save for the corrupted figure in one duplicate copy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Negative definition with the 72-hour aggregation rule; convoluted but complete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence saving provision; clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Punitive damages exclusion repeated verbatim; a single clear rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A second copy of an endorsement already attached, redundancy without contradiction.
